description: The clean cross-isotope C_knot universality test, run with the NOW-PINNED Markov weight y_λ (PR #4543, Σ y_λ f^λ = 1 verified). Master-formula conventions (binding_energy_categorical_deuteron): B(K) = m_e·|Σ_λ y_λ χ^λ(β_K) sgn f^λ|, χ^λ from the interface-inclusive Rust Hoefsmit caches. Result: C_knot = 5.85/4.44/3.29/9.31 for D/T/³He/⁴He → spread 2.83×, NON-UNIVERSAL. f^λ (hook SYT) is the tightest dim convention (2.83× vs dim_q 116×, none 122×); no global/A-power scale fixes it (log C/log A non-constant); a deuteron-pinned 0-fit scale mispredicts T/³He/⁴He by +32%/+78%/−37% (≫ isospin ±8%). Mirror pair T & ³He at the SAME H₉ need C_knot differing 35% (robust 1.29–1.35 across dim conventions) ⇒ C_knot is NOT a function of (n,q₀); it is per-knot Δ_λ. scope-(a): single-universal-C_knot derivation route REFUTED; scope-(b): level-only rescale g(n,q₀) excluded by the mirror inequality (Lean cknot_level_only_excluded). Δ_λ magnitude stays OPEN (bean qou-3q7t). Supersedes c_knot_not_universal_probe.py (whose 41× was right-vs-wrong weight, now resolved). No fit; B_AME diagnostic-only (never inverted); nothing wired; exact mpmath.
